title: José Study · current design frontier 2026-09-11
human_intent: Continue the José algebra study engine from the current chat-built V11 frontier without falling back to older chat demos. Preserve the canonical 48-exercise course while improving the student-facing hierarchy, theory/practice flow, map, tactile interaction and responsive layout.
already_decided: The course has an abstract Algebra menu with four separate topics: Index Laws, Factorization, Quadratics and Simultaneous Equations.
Entering one topic opens a topic-local map of 12 levels grouped into three rounds; the left rail must never represent all four course topics at once.
The canonical 48 exercises come from pages/JOSE_RECUPERACION_ALGEBRA_FINAL.html; do not replace them with simplified invented exercises.
Theory and the topic-local map move together conceptually, but theory scrolling must not silently change or destroy the current practice state.
On small screens theory is the primary surface and practice is a collapsible three-snap bottom sheet; opening the board expands practice while preserving context.
Desktop must preserve touch-like interaction parity: wheel/trackpad plus click-drag and pen-drag scroll on product surfaces; the board remains draw-on-drag.
Selection is not submission; distractors are diagnostic and traps are not announced before the exercise.
Normal four-option multiple choice should fit as one composition without requiring avoidable scrolling on a small phone.
Sound defaults on; exact two-color Prometeo palette switching remains available.
The left map must feel like a designed product, not a compressed system list: strong round separation, readable current level, more air and reduced inactive-label noise.
useful_delta: V7 corrected the architecture into course menu -> one topic -> 12 topic-local levels -> exercise.
V8 added mouse/pen grab-scroll parity with touch.
V9 removed unnecessary helper/engine text, stopped revealing traps and compacted MCQ layout.
V10 fixed actual nested-overflow geometry so touchpad/wheel and click-drag scrolling work rather than only having gesture code.
V11 widened and refined the left map, increased round separation and breathing room, emphasized the active node and introduced compact map labels.
known_failures: Do not resume from V4 or another older demo merely because it is easy to locate.
Do not collapse all four algebra topics into one map rail.
Do not compress the map into tiny dense labels and dots.
Do not add explanatory filler such as 'seguí bajando', engine metadata or visible trap labels.
Do not make four standard MCQ options so tall that the student must scroll just to compare them.
Do not implement desktop drag-scroll without first constraining the nested scroll containers to real viewport heights.
Do not treat a saved lab frontier as Human Accepted, Current or Served.
Do not fork shared Study CSS/JS into the student-specific product merely to continue the design.
authority_boundary: This workstream stores a resumable LAB frontier only. It does not modify Catalog, Current, Lineage, Human Accepted or Served pointers and grants no promotion authority.
next_best_action: Continue design critique from V11, especially the topic-local left map and density, while preserving every settled interaction and course-architecture decision above.
